catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class binds a whole-protocol upload and run on a lab.liquid_handler. The cap.fluid.* classes address a declared labware well, while the upstream run interface accepts a protocol file and exposes no well-targeted aspirate or dispense command.
No catalogue class binds a run stop on a lab.liquid_handler. The cap.fluid.* classes describe aspirate, dispense, transfer and mix operations; none stops an executing protocol run.

notes:
Gate passed on the fake backend with G8 warning SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names PythonObjectDriver, but the upstream interface is a stateful HTTP protocol runner. transfer returns a run id that the native stop path needs, and a fixed bridge command map cannot carry that dynamic id into the e-stop. driver.py is therefore a direct Driver over ot2_interface.ot2_driver_http:OT2_Driver (the card entry symbol), with a package fake. The primary control is preserved: x-cap.ad-sdl.start_protocol.v1 uploads a protocol file through native transfer, creates the run and starts it through native resume (the play action). Reads expose robot_status, runs, active_run_id and active_run_status. x-cap.ad-sdl.stop_active_run.v1 (safe_state=True, no input) and the @estop post native cancel, which is the robot run stop action. When the driver has no run of its own, the stop path first reads native get_runs and cancels every run the robot reports as running, paused or finishing, so a run started elsewhere is also targeted. The stop is an acknowledged request, not sensed quiescence: the clone neither waits for the stopped state nor reports it, so the safe-state output says stop-requested. The clone's get_runs has no request timeout, so a silent network can delay the stop path; the robot's own controls remain authoritative. Not covered: cap.fluid.aspirate.v1 and cap.fluid.dispense.v1 are not bound because the clone exposes no well-targeted pipetting command; its streaming example only loads labware and moves a pipette relative (tests/test_ot2_streaming.py:12-65). Pause and resume are not separate MHS actions; the primary protocol-run start is exposed and the runtime e-stop covers the stop. The upstream execute() loop is not used because it catches every exception and has no timeout (src/ot2_interface/ot2_driver_http.py:197-210). No numeric input is exposed, so there are no Limits and no site overlay; the clone states no volume, speed or duration bound for a protocol. Fake fidelity: fake.py is an analytic in-memory stand-in, not a recording and not the Opentrons simulator. It does not open or compile the protocol path, although the real backend uploads a readable local file. Its generated protocol and run ids are placeholders, its F0 time is immediate method return rather than robot protocol timing, and it has no physical motion. Hardware: no hardware backend was run and no hardware was attached. The package is model-authored and reviewed_by is null; at R2 the loader refuses the hardware backend until a human signs it. The clone documents no independent hardware e-stop, so estop_physical_ref is not set and SAFE-045 is met by the input-free safe-state action. This stop is a software run stop over the robot HTTP API, not a safety-rated channel. G8 warned SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE because no actuating limit exists to probe; every other CL3 test passed.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Fix: the gate passed as recorded, but the stop path was unconfirmed: the e-stop and the safe-state action posted cancel without checking its answer or the run state, cancelled a kept own run id instead of the runs actually moving, reported completed when GET /runs did not answer (get_runs() or []), and used upstream calls without a timeout; start_protocol also uploaded any host file and reported completed when the robot refused play. driver.py now lists GET /runs and sends the stop action (the request cancel builds, through the upstream send_request with a 5 s timeout, the package's choice) to every run running, paused, finishing or in a status the clone does not name, and to its own new run while the play is in flight, confirms each by a fresh read (stop-requested, stopped, succeeded or failed) or raises SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held; protocol_path is Limit.operator_required (the operator lists the allowed protocol files; example in the new site-limits.example.json); a non-201 play fails MHS.DEVICE.FAULTED with its code, a raising play or unreadable started run is unknown, the runs read fails instead of returning [], the safe-state output is stopped_runs, and Facts were corrected (resume, cancel, OT2Node.cancel, reset_robot_data) and added (201, send_request, light switching at construction, prints, timeouts, Flex, module and gripper commands). fake.py follows the upstream answers and send_request routes with refusals and stop-requested timing as placeholders; native.py's docstring now says opening the backend switches the lights; test_driver.py adds ten cases (refused, ignored and unanswered stops, a run started elsewhere, a play in flight during the e-stop, refused and raising play, the allowlist) and seven mutants of the new rules are each caught; facts.md was rewritten, reference.json and REFERENCE.md regenerated, check-report.json rewritten by the gate. Superseded author notes: there is no DEVIATION FROM THE CARD (the card's decision is direct-driver), the stop is confirmed by state, the package now has an operator-required limit and an example overlay, and the G8 SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE warning is gone; G1-G9 pass with no finding, risk stays R2, and RESULT.json, driver.lock.json and task.json are unchanged. For the human reviewer: (1) Allow in site-limits.json only protocol files a person reviewed: the envelope bounds which file runs, not what it does (volumes, temperature modules, protopiler/config.py:262-268, the Flex gripper, :271-272); the path match is exact and the file content stays the operator's; biological or hazardous samples make it R3 by the hazard table. (2) The stop is a run stop over the HTTP API: stop-requested means accepted, not that motion ended; it does not reset module set points (whether the robot does is not in the clone); runs another client starts after the listing and anything outside a run are not covered; the clone documents no hardware e-stop, so know the robot's own stop before use. (3) A run continues after start_protocol returns and after the session ends. (4) The 5 s request timeout and the default 1 s e-stop budget are not sourced: on a slow robot the e-stop receipt can fail and the background retry confirm later. (5) Opening the backend switches the lights after a probe without timeout; transfer, check_run_status and get_run print to stdout, which corrupts a stdio endpoint. (6) robot_status mirrors the upstream: an older stopped or failed run can hide a running one. (7) Upstream stream/_stream passes max_retries to requests.post, which requests does not accept, so it raises at the pin (unused here). (8) The package says OT-2; the upstream also targets the Flex (README.md:3) over the same API: confirm the model.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-sonnet-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Adversarial verification of the claude-opus-5-5 review (fix) by a different model (the user chose Claude Sonnet as the different model, 2026-11-04): the verifier agreed and found no blocker or major. No blocker or major found. I re-ran the gate: G1-G9 pass, digest sha256:265efb6b... matches the reviewer's. I re-ran collect.py --strict: PASS, with only RESULT_DIGEST_STALE, which the orchestrator fixes. show_refs.py reports 0 bad citations, and I read all 23 cited ranges against the pinned clone; each says what its Fact claims. The stop path lists GET /runs, stops every non-rest run, and confirms each with a fresh read. If GET /runs is unanswered, or a stop is not confirmed, it raises SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED. The reviewer's earlier `get_runs() or []` hole is closed. protocol_path is operator_required, the example overlay is labelled as an example, the licence is MIT, and the risk class R2 is disclosed with the R3 caveat. The remaining points are minor.
